landing.headline: Every match,
landing.sub: A probability engine for the Big Five leagues and the European competitions. 1X2, goals, corners, cards and player markets — all read off one score distribution, so they can never contradict each other.
landing.heroNote: Fitted on {matches} matches across {seasons} seasons. Odds are never an input — only the yardstick.

benchmark.title: How close to the sharpest price on the market
benchmark.lead: Ranked probability score on {sample} Big Five matches, 2020/21–2025/26, against Bet365's closing odds. Lower is better.
benchmark.conclusion: Between knowing nothing and the best-informed price on the market there is {gap} of RPS. The engine covers {coverage} of it.
benchmark.caveat: It does not beat the closing line, and it is not sold as if it did. The gap holds in every season and every league, which is what makes it a ceiling rather than noise.
benchmark.axis: Bar length is the share of the distance covered, from no information at all to the closing price. The figure on the right is the raw RPS.

markets.title: One distribution, thirty markets
markets.lead: Each market is read off the same simulated score distribution. That is why the over/under never disagrees with the correct score, and the team totals always add up.
markets.matchDesc: 1X2, double chance, draw no bet, exact score matrix
markets.goalsDesc: Over/under from 0.5 to 5.5, both teams to score, half-time lines
markets.teamDesc: Corners, cards, fouls, shots and shots on target — total and per side
markets.playerDesc: Anytime scorer, shots, assists, cards, with penalty-taker weighting

proof.title: Predictions are written down before kick-off
proof.lead: Every prediction is timestamped and stored before the match is played, then settled against the real result. A track record that cannot be edited after the fact is the only kind worth showing.
proof.point1: Each season is predicted using only what was known before it started. No model ever sees the match it is grading.
proof.point2: Bookmaker prices are used to measure the engine, never to train it. Otherwise the benchmark would be measuring itself.
proof.point3: Results, shots and lineups from public sources. No paid feeds, no insider information, no scraping behind a login.

cta.title: See it on this weekend's fixtures
cta.lead: Every match of the round, priced before it is played.
cta.note: No account needed. Nothing to install.

footer.disclaimer: For analysis and entertainment. Not betting advice. 18+.

preview.title: A real fixture, priced by the engine

preview.b1: Result, expected goals, over/under and both teams to score — all read off the same distribution.
preview.b2: The likeliest scorelines, ranked, with the probability attached to each.
preview.b3: Corners, cards, fouls and player markets sit one click deeper.

match.scorersNote: Probability of scoring at least once, given the player features. Bars are scaled to the leader: the model never puts anyone above about 35%, so the ranking is the signal, not the absolute height.

match.noData: This match's data hasn't been ingested yet.

match.rangeNote: ✓ means the real value landed inside the range we called most likely; the % is the probability we gave it.

match.metaPlayed: {home} {score} {away} — the result next to what our model predicted before kick-off.

results.liveLead: Every prediction is timestamped and written down before the match is played, then settled against the real result. Nothing is added afterwards.
results.honestNote: An honest model is right about as often as it says it will be. Far above what it announced is luck; far below is a problem.
results.noSettled: Predictions are committed and waiting for the matches to be played. Settled results will appear here.

calibration.lead: Thousands of out-of-sample 1X2 selections, grouped by the probability announced.
calibration.ece: Average calibration error: {value}. Below 0.02 is considered excellent.

leagues.title: How every league ends
leagues.lead: The title, the Champions League places and the drop, simulated ten thousand times from where the season actually stands.
leagues.headline: {team} is the title favourite at {p}%, with {remaining} matches left in the season.
leagues.raceNote: Bars scaled to the favourite. Ten thousand simulations of the remaining fixtures, from the real table.
leagues.tableNote: {leader} leads. xPts is the points total the simulation expects each team to reach by the final day, over the {remaining} matches still to be played.
leagues.matrixLead: Each row is a team, each column a finishing position, and each cell how often the simulation put them there. Blank means under half a percent.
leagues.metaDesc: {league}: {team} is the title favourite at {p}%. Simulated from the current table.
leagues.offlineBody: The engine fits itself from 45,938 matches when it first starts. Give it a minute and reload.

competitions.title: Champions, Europa, Conference
competitions.lead: The Swiss league phase, the playoff and every knockout round, simulated two thousand times from where the competition actually stands.
competitions.headline: {team} is the favourite at {p}%, with {played} of {total} league-phase matches played.
competitions.preDraw: The draw has not been made yet. The field below is estimated from the Elo ranking and every simulation draws its own valid league phase — treat the participants as a guess, not a list.
competitions.raceNote: Bars scaled to the favourite. {sims} simulations of the whole format: league phase, playoff, two-legged ties with extra time and penalties, and a single final on neutral ground.
competitions.methodNote: Strengths come from ClubElo, a single European scale, with an Elo-to-goals mapping calibrated on 20,000 of this project’s own matches. Cross-league fixtures are why: a model fitted league by league cannot say whether a good Dutch side beats a mid-table Italian one.
competitions.metaDesc: {competition}: {team} is the favourite at {p}%. Simulated from the current state of the competition.
competitions.offlineBody: It needs the current ClubElo ratings and the published calendar. Give it a moment and reload.

awards.title: The Golden Boot race
awards.lead: Who finishes as the league’s leading scorer, simulated twenty thousand times over every fixture still to be played.
awards.computing: Walking every remaining fixture through the player model. The first look at a league takes about half a minute; after that it is instant.
awards.methodNote: Bars scaled to the favourite. Each player’s goals in each remaining fixture come from the player model, conditioned on the goals his team is expected to score in that specific match — so a striker with eight games left is not compared with one who has two.
awards.offlineBody: The engine fits itself from 45,938 matches when it first starts. Give it a minute and reload.

mode.sandboxLead: Any eleven you like, no constraints, from any league.
